name: AIGMos Canonical Contract Format
purpose: Define the representation-independent canonical semantic contract model and the deterministic reading rules required to reconstruct AIGMos structure, topics, authority, behavior and explicit causality without semantic guessing.

bootstrap.rule: Load this root Contract Format first, then load the exact Canonical Master. Recursively scan canonical/json/** only to discover candidate documents. The active canonical source set is the exact set declared by Master.active_contract_refs plus the already-loaded Master, subject to allowed source_role and one-id/one-active-definition validation. Filesystem presence alone never creates authority. Master.active_root_refs define semantic entry surfaces inside that active set.

representation.rule: JSON is a serialization format only. JSON is not the semantic standard.
representation.round_trip_goal: representation A -> canonical semantic model -> representation B MUST preserve semantic identity and all required meaning.

fundamental_rules.rule: Active semantics MUST NOT be inferred from prose, filenames, directory placement, naming convention, array position, visual placement, implementation behavior or software-specific heuristics.
Every fact required to reconstruct active canonical structure MUST be explicit structured data.
Execution order, branching, continuation and causality that matter to behavior MUST be explicit structured flow data.
A Topic is a recursive grouping construct. Topic membership MUST NOT imply containment, ownership, authority, dependency or causality.
A Topic MUST be declared under the semantic parent node to which its subject naturally belongs. Topics MUST NOT require a separate global topics directory.
A Topic MAY reference canonical identities anywhere in the tree when the subject crosses architectural boundaries.
Topics are created according to semantic usefulness, not scarcity. A new Topic SHOULD be created when an existing Topic would require semantic stretching.
Unknown or missing semantics MUST be reported as gaps and MUST NOT be invented.
One active semantic identity MUST resolve to exactly one active semantic definition.
A valid contract MUST survive representation -> normalized canonical semantic model -> representation without semantic invention or loss.
A canonical semantic identity MAY belong to multiple Topics simultaneously. Multiple Topic memberships are valid and expected when the identity participates in multiple subject groupings.

Topics MAY inherit parent Topics recursively. Membership in a child Topic implies grouping membership in every inherited ancestor Topic, but Topic inheritance MUST NOT transfer ownership, authority, dependency, containment or causality.

An active canonical semantic identity with no direct or inherited Topic membership MUST be explicitly marked as an Outsider with a machine-readable reason. Zero Topic membership without explicit Outsider status is invalid.

A Topic MAY be composed from existing Topics. Topic composition reuses existing grouping and trace surfaces by reference; it MUST NOT duplicate or transfer their semantics. A mechanism specification SHOULD describe only additional mechanism-specific semantics and explicit causality.

lifecycle.unlocked: Active canonical semantics exist but have not passed the current Contract Format validation or contain an unresolved semantic, topic, reference or traceability gap.
lifecycle.locked: The current Contract Format, deterministic reference resolution, topic reachability, semantic closure, traceability and all applicable hard gates have passed.
lifecycle.superseded: Historical/reference record; not an active semantic definition.
lifecycle.deprecated: Compatibility/history record; not active for new canonical work.
lifecycle.format_migration: A breaking Contract Format change MUST unlock every affected active contract until individually revalidated.

identity.rule: id is the stable semantic identity and MUST originate from explicit structured canonical identity data.

members.rule: members defines semantic identities owned inside this contract. External identities belong in references, topics or structure edges.

structure.rule: Containment, relation, ownership, authority and dependency are separate semantic dimensions.

topics.placement_rule: Topics are declared inside the semantic parent contract/node whose subject area naturally contains the Topic.
topics.directory_rule: A separate global /topics directory is neither required nor semantically authoritative.

topic_semantics.name: Human-readable Topic name.
topic_semantics.purpose: What end-to-end subject or grouping this Topic represents.
topic_semantics.member_refs: Canonical semantic identities participating in this Topic.
topic_semantics.child_topics: Nested Topics recursively belonging under this Topic.
topic_semantics.parent_topic_refs: Zero or more parent Topic identities inherited recursively. Parent Topics provide grouping context only.
topic_semantics.composed_topic_refs: Zero or more existing Topic identities whose already-defined grouping/trace surfaces are reused as components of this Topic. Composition reuses definitions; it does not copy or transfer their semantics.

rules: Topic is a grouping and trace construct, not a semantic owner.
Topic membership is many-to-many.
The same canonical identity MAY participate in multiple Topics simultaneously.
A Topic MAY inherit zero or more parent Topics through explicit parent_topic_refs.
Topic inheritance is recursive.
Membership in a child Topic implies grouping membership in all inherited ancestor Topics.
A Topic MAY compose zero or more existing Topics through explicit composed_topic_refs.
Topic composition and Topic inheritance are different relations and MUST NOT be conflated.
Inheritance means the Topic belongs under and inherits grouping context from its parent Topic or Topics.
Composition means the Topic reuses existing Topic grouping/trace surfaces as components of a new mechanism or subject.
A composed Topic MUST reference existing Topics rather than duplicate their already-defined semantics.
A composed Topic SHOULD add only mechanism-specific members, relations, operations, events, flows, conditions or causality not already represented by its component Topics.
Topic composition MAY cross canonical branches.
Topic composition MAY be recursive but MUST resolve deterministically and MUST NOT contain unresolved composition cycles.
Topic inheritance and composition do not transfer semantic ownership.
Topic inheritance and composition do not grant runtime or policy authority.
Topic inheritance and composition do not create dependency.
Topic inheritance and composition do not create semantic containment.
Topic inheritance and composition do not define execution order or causality.
Execution order and causality that are specific to a composed mechanism MUST remain explicit behavior.flows data.
Topic membership does not replace explicit structure edges or explicit flows.
A broad Topic such as Runtime MAY parent more specific Topics such as Automation, Symbols, Queues, UserModules, Tools, I/O and AI runtime.
A specific Topic such as Trigger MAY inherit Runtime -> Automation while the same canonical identities MAY simultaneously participate in other Topic branches such as Core.
A mechanism Topic such as Order Creation MAY compose existing Topics from multiple branches and add only the end-to-end causality specific to creating an order.
A Topic SHOULD be located at the nearest semantically correct parent from which the subject is naturally discoverable by recursion.
Topics are not scarce. Create a new Topic when an existing Topic would require semantic stretching.
When adding a new subject, ask first: does this belong under an existing Topic, or should a new Topic be created?
When describing a mechanism, ask next: can this mechanism be composed from existing Topics, with only its new causality specified locally?
An identity is not an Outsider when it has either direct Topic membership or inherited Topic membership through a child Topic.
topics.coverage_rule: Every active non-bootstrap canonical semantic identity MUST have at least one direct or inherited Topic membership, OR it MUST be explicitly marked outsider=true with an outsider_reason. Zero Topic membership without explicit Outsider status is a hard failure.

example.name: Order Creation
example.purpose: Describe the end-to-end order creation mechanism by composing existing canonical Topic surfaces and adding only order-creation-specific causality.

metadata.note: Existing Topic semantics are reused by reference. FLOW_ORDER_CREATION carries only the causality specific to the end-to-end creation mechanism.

outsider_contract.purpose: Represent unresolved Topic classification visibly without forcing an incorrect Topic assignment.

fields.outsider: boolean; true only when no direct or inherited Topic membership is currently resolved
fields.outsider_reason: machine-readable explanation of why Topic classification is unresolved

rules: Outsider is a classification status, not a Topic.
Outsider MUST NOT be implemented as a separate global directory.
Outsider MUST remain visible to generic readers and validators.
Once a valid direct or inherited Topic membership exists, outsider MUST be false or absent.

composition_contract.purpose: Allow mechanism and subject specifications to reuse already-defined Topic surfaces without duplicating documentation or semantics.
composition_contract.principle: Define once -> inherit Topics -> compose Topics -> describe only the new causality.
rules: composed_topic_refs MUST resolve to existing Topic identities.
Composition MUST NOT copy canonical semantics merely to make the composed Topic self-contained.
Composition MUST NOT reinterpret the semantics of a referenced Topic.
Composition MUST NOT imply runtime execution order.
Mechanism-specific ordering, branching, conditions, continuation and causality MUST be explicit in referenced or local flows.
A composed Topic MAY add direct member_refs and trace refs when the mechanism contains genuinely additional participants.
If required semantics cannot be expressed by existing Topics plus explicit mechanism-specific causality, the missing semantics are a canonical gap and MUST NOT be guessed.
composition_contract.documentation_effect: A mechanism specification can be expressed by composing existing Topics and declaring only the mechanism-specific causality or additional semantics. Existing semantic documentation is referenced, not duplicated.

flow_rules: Execution causality MUST come from explicit flow data.
Dependency MUST NOT define execution order.
Containment MUST NOT define execution order.
Ownership MUST NOT define execution order.
Authority MUST NOT define execution order.
Topic membership MUST NOT define execution order.
Branches MUST carry explicit conditions and continuations.
A flow MUST NOT itself grant runtime authority.

semantics.rule: Contract-specific structured semantics that are not identity, graph structure, Topic grouping, behavior, constraints, references or prose live here.
semantics.reference_rule: A value whose meaning is a reference to another canonical identity MUST use references, topics, structure or behavior records instead of an unresolved name/path.

references.rule: Every active target_ref MUST resolve to exactly one active semantic identity.

prose.rule: Prose may explain semantics but MUST NOT be the only carrier of a machine-significant structural, Topic, authority, behavioral or causal fact.

reader_algorithm.purpose: Define how a generic consumer reads the canonical tree without AIGMos-specific guessing.

steps.rule: Load the canonical Master and use only explicit identities and references to discover active roots.
Resolve each active id to exactly one active definition.
Read scope, members, structure and contract-specific semantics as separate dimensions.

Read Topics directly under the current semantic node, recursively read child_topics, resolve parent_topic_refs and inherited ancestor Topic memberships, resolve composed_topic_refs as reusable Topic trace components, and resolve every referenced canonical identity without changing semantic ownership or structural parent.
Resolve composed_topic_refs recursively. Reuse their resolved grouping/trace surfaces by reference. Do not copy semantics and do not infer execution order from composition.
Read states, interfaces, operations, events and flows.
Use only explicit flow steps for execution order, branching, continuation and causality.
Confirm that every active non-bootstrap semantic identity has at least one direct or inherited Topic membership, or is explicitly marked outsider=true with outsider_reason.
Verify that normalization and reverse serialization preserve active semantic meaning.

forbidden_reader_behaviors: infer identity from filename
infer semantic parent from directory path
infer Topic membership from directory path
infer ownership from Topic membership
infer authority from Topic membership
infer dependency from Topic membership
infer causality from Topic membership
infer execution order from array position
invent missing references
invent missing Topics
treat Topic inheritance as ownership inheritance
treat Topic inheritance as authority inheritance
treat Topic inheritance as dependency inheritance
treat Topic inheritance as causal inheritance
hide zero-membership identities instead of exposing Outsider status
infer execution order from composed_topic_refs
copy semantics from composed Topics into the composing Topic
treat Topic composition as ownership transfer
treat Topic composition as authority transfer
treat Topic composition as dependency

traceability.reverse_trace: Higher-level action or Topic -> explicit lower-level canonical semantic, platform and runtime mechanisms.
traceability.forward_trace: Foundational mechanism -> Topics, operations, flows and higher-level semantics that explicitly reference it.
traceability.topic_trace: Topic -> parent_topic_refs + composed_topic_refs + child_topics + direct trace refs -> inherited grouping context + composed reusable trace surfaces + resolved canonical identities.
traceability.projector_test: A generic Structure Projector MUST be able to recursively reconstruct nodes and Topics, then traverse a Topic end-to-end without embedded AIGMos-specific semantic guessing.
traceability.mechanism_trace: Mechanism Topic -> composed existing Topics -> mechanism-specific operations/events/flows -> explicit end-to-end causality. Existing semantics are not duplicated.

canonicalization.ordered_array_rule: If array order carries semantics, its owning field MUST explicitly declare ordered=true.
canonicalization.required_empty_dimensions: Required dimensions remain present as empty arrays or objects when applicable but empty.

round_trip.forward: representation -> normalized canonical semantic model MUST preserve identities, structure, Topics, behavior, flows, semantics, constraints and references.
round_trip.reverse: normalized canonical semantic model -> representation MUST invent nothing and drop nothing.
round_trip.equivalence: Whitespace, JSON key order and non-semantic serialization details may differ; semantic meaning may not.

validator.lock_rule: lock_eligible=true permits unlocked -> locked. Otherwise the contract MUST remain unlocked.

hard_gates.condition: A required format field or semantic dimension is absent.
One identity has multiple active definitions.
An active reference resolves to zero active identities.
An active reference resolves to multiple active identities.
An active non-bootstrap canonical semantic identity has no direct or inherited Topic membership and is not explicitly marked outsider=true with outsider_reason.
A new subject has no resolved placement under an existing Topic and no explicit new Topic has been defined.
Topic identity, membership or semantic parent must be inferred from a filesystem directory or filename.
Containment, ownership, authority, dependency or causality is inferred from Topic membership.
Execution order, branching, continuation or causality must be inferred from dependency, containment, ownership, authority, Topic membership, visual position or prose.
A generic canonical consumer requires AIGMos-specific heuristic interpretation to reconstruct significant active semantics.
Representation -> canonical semantic model -> representation changes active semantic meaning.
An active identity has outsider=true but outsider_reason is absent or empty.
An active identity is marked outsider=true while a direct or inherited Topic membership resolves.
Topic parent inheritance contains an unresolved cycle that prevents deterministic ancestor membership resolution.
Ownership, authority, dependency, containment or causality is inherited solely because of Topic parent inheritance.
A composed_topic_ref resolves to zero or multiple active Topic identities.
Topic composition contains an unresolved recursive cycle that prevents deterministic resolution.
A composing Topic duplicates already-defined canonical semantics solely to restate a referenced component Topic.
Execution order or causality is inferred solely from composed_topic_refs instead of explicit flow data.
Ownership, authority, dependency or containment is transferred solely because one Topic composes another.

migration.rule: All affected active contracts MUST be unlocked until the required topics dimension, Topic coverage and 1.4 reader/traceability rules pass.
migration.topic_migration_rule: Do not create a global Topic directory. Place Topics under their semantically correct parent nodes. Permit multiple simultaneous Topic memberships, recursive parent inheritance and explicit Topic composition. Reuse existing Topics through composed_topic_refs instead of duplicating their semantics. Mechanism Topics add only genuinely new semantics and explicit mechanism-specific causality. If an active identity has no direct or inherited Topic membership, expose it as outsider=true with outsider_reason instead of guessing.

final_lock: A generic consumer can start from Master, recursively reconstruct canonical nodes and locally declared Topics, resolve multiple memberships, parent inheritance and Topic composition, expose unresolved zero-membership identities as Outsiders, reuse existing Topic trace surfaces without semantic duplication, reconstruct mechanism-specific behavior and explicit causality, and validate the complete semantic model without path-based or AIGMos-specific guessing.
